meta.title: Muse Wonder
meta.thesis: Muse Wonder is built to remember you, and keep going until the job is done.

narration.say: Meta has a new model? What's it for?

narration: Muse Wonder is Meta's new model for agents: AI that does tasks for you, at work and at home.
Two ideas carry it. The first, Meta calls Active Memory.
It keeps what matters about you from past chats.
And when a new task needs it, it pulls that detail back up on its own.
The second is Active Focus: staying on a hard goal.
When it hits a blocker, it tries another way instead of giving up.
And before an important step, it checks with you first.

narration.say: Don't all new models top the tests?

narration: That's the catch. Two models can score the same on tests, and still differ on tasks they've never seen.
Meta plotted both: tasks it practised for, against tasks it never saw.
The new model sits above the old model's line: on new tasks, it does better than its test scores predict.
Meta says that's because it's built on a bigger, stronger base model.

narration.say: So it remembers me, keeps at it, and handles new stuff.

narration: Developers can use it today, through Meta's Model API and Muse Code.
A second version, called Full, is for Muse Code subscribers.
It comes to the Muse app soon, subscribers first.

narration.say: An agent with my messages and calendar? Is that safe?

narration: Meta says it's trained to resist bad instructions, and to be careful with private information.
A full safety report is coming soon.
So Muse Wonder is built to remember you, and keep going until the job is done.
